query: I want to buy my first electric vehicle. Which EV should I get?
sources:
Source 1 (2023, Consumer Reports, USA): The Tesla Model 3 remains the top-rated EV for first-time buyers — best-in-class range, extensive Supercharger network, and strong owner satisfaction make it the default recommendation despite higher price.

Source 2 (2022, The Verge, USA): The Chevrolet Equinox EV (arriving 2024) and Volkswagen ID.4 offer federal tax credit eligibility that effectively reduces the purchase price by $7,500 — making them compelling value propositions versus non-credit-eligible vehicles.

Source 3 (2023, Reddit r/electricvehicles, Global): Community advice for first-time EV buyers: prioritize charging network access over specs — Tesla's Supercharger network is the most reliable for road trips; other brands have improved but still lag on long-distance charging confidence.

Source 4 (2022, RTINGS, Canada): The Hyundai Ioniq 6 offers exceptional range (up to 361 miles) and ultra-fast 800V charging at competitive pricing — the best non-Tesla option for buyers who do occasional long road trips.

Source 5 (2021, Electrek, USA): Home charging setup is the most important factor first-time EV buyers underestimate — 80% of EV charging happens at home, and buyers without a Level 2 charger installation will find ownership significantly more inconvenient.
atoms: perspective: Budget-conscious buyer maximizing tax credit value
perspective: First-time EV buyer prioritizing ease and reliability
plausible_answers: Get a Tesla Model 3, since the Supercharger network, range, and ownership experience make it the most reliable first EV.
Choose the Hyundai Ioniq 6 for range and speed, since 361 miles and 800V ultra-fast charging rival Tesla for less.
Buy a tax-credit-eligible EV like the Chevy Equinox EV or VW ID.4, since the $7,500 federal credit meaningfully cuts price.
